name: The Isms That Made the Modern World
description: Liberalism, socialism, nationalism, communism, fascism and more: where each political idea came from, who argued for it and how it changed the way countries are run.

checkpoints.name: Old answers about power
checkpoints.note: Long before modern parties, Chinese thinkers argued whether rulers should govern by moral example or by strict law. Their debate between Confucians and Legalists shaped a state that lasted for two millennia.

checkpoints.name: Reason and rights
checkpoints.note: In Britain and France, writers claim that people have natural rights and that governments rule by consent. Locke's ideas feed liberalism, and Adam Smith's account of markets leads to capitalism.

checkpoints.name: Age of revolutions
checkpoints.note: Revolution in France brings new ideas and a backlash against them. Conservatives, nationalists, feminists, socialists and anarchists each answer the same question: how should society be organised.

checkpoints.name: Marx and the masses
checkpoints.note: Karl Marx and Engels publish the Communist Manifesto, and workers' parties grow. At the end of the century Zionism and Pan-Africanism show nationalism spreading to peoples without states of their own.

checkpoints.name: Ideologies in power
checkpoints.note: After the First World War, fascism takes power in Italy and elsewhere, and communist states are established. The long contest between these ideas and liberal democracy defines much of the twentieth century.
